title: GTA 6 Changes the Sprint Button After 25 Years
description: After nearly 25 years, Grand Theft Auto 6 is changing how sprinting works, finally moving away from the traditional button-tapping mechanic for running.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## GTA 6 Changes the Sprint Button After 25 Years

For nearly 25 years, Grand Theft Auto games have uniquely mapped your sprint movement to a face button on a controller. Across multiple console generations, the default control scheme for Rockstar Games' flagship franchise has consistently required players to rhythmically tap either the X or the A button—depending on your platform—just to get your character to sprint across the map. It has long been an iconic, if sometimes fatiguing, staple of the series' physical control input.

However, according to recent reports from gaming outlet Eurogamer, GTA 6 is finally bucking this long-standing trend.

### Moving Away From a 25-Year Tradition

While some historical Rockstar Games titles have offered alternative control layouts over the years, the default method for running in GTA has stubbornly remained tied to face button tapping for a quarter of a century. As the gaming landscape evolved and contemporary open-world action titles standardized more ergonomic, fluid movement controls utilizing thumbsticks and modern layouts, the classic GTA control scheme stood out as a relic of an older era.

By stepping away from this tradition in GTA 6, the developers are signaling a modern approach to player movement and comfort. Navigating the expansive environments and dense urban landscapes of the game's next-generation world will likely feel drastically different when players are no longer required to endlessly mash a controller button to keep up their momentum.

### Impact on Player Experience

For veteran fans, unlearning a muscle memory built over decades might take a brief adjustment period. Yet, for both newcomers and returning players alike, eliminating the mandatory face-button tapping routine represents a welcome quality-of-life update that aligns the franchise with modern gaming standards.

## Editor's Take

It is fascinating to see a massive franchise like GTA willingness to alter something as fundamental as its sprint input after 25 years. While it is just one piece of the wider control scheme puzzle, this change highlights a thoughtful approach to modernizing player interaction for the next major entry.
